title: Automated Secure Proxy for Micro-SaaS
business: A boutique micro-SaaS provider managing multiple independent web applications and internal microservices.
problem: Manual certificate management and complex Nginx configurations lead to frequent downtime during certificate renewals and routing errors when scaling services.
solution: Caddy automates HTTPS certificate provisioning via ACME protocol and simplifies routing through a declarative Caddyfile, allowing the provider to serve static assets and proxy traffic to backend services with minimal overhead.
steps: Install the Caddy binary on the host server.
Define the domain names in the Caddyfile to trigger automatic TLS.
Use the file_server directive to serve static frontend assets.
Configure the reverse_proxy directive to route API traffic to internal ports.
Reload the configuration using the Caddy API or system service restart.
outcome: The provider achieves zero-touch SSL management and a human-readable configuration format that reduces the risk of manual routing errors.
limitation: Caddy performs automatic certificate management which requires port 80/443 access; if the server is behind a restrictive firewall or lacks public DNS resolution, the ACME challenge will fail, requiring manual certificate handling.
